An unconventional, no-bullshit guide to forging a rewarding career that matches your passions in the world—from a leading venture capitalist, based on his viral college talk.
 Venture capitalist Bill Gurley came very close to “career regret.” A computer science major, he first landed a job at one of the most prominent tech companies in the country. It should have been a dream come true—but he was soon bored. He left the industry and started again from scratch, first at business school, then on Wall Street, and finally in Silicon Valley, where he went on to spend two decades in venture capital.

...

Pulling from Gurley’s own experience and extensive contacts across a wide range of industries—from talent agent Lorrie Bartlett to restauranteur Danny Meyer, who epitomize these principles and have reached the top of their fields while loving what they do—as well as his original research on career regret, Runnin’ Down the Dream identifies six key principles for flourishing, purpose-filled careers:
1. Chase your curiosity
2. Hone your craft
3. Develop mentors in your field
4. Embrace your peers
5. Go where the action is
6. Always give back

## Plot Summary

Bill Gurley, a veteran venture capitalist and general partner at Benchmark, a leading Silicon Valley investment firm, opens by challenging the assumption that people who thrive in their dream jobs got there through luck or special access. He argues that deliberate, replicable principles matter far more than fortune, framing the problem through what he calls the "conveyor belt": a system in which young people are pushed toward high-paying careers with little regard for fulfillment.

...

Gurley structures the book as alternating profiles of people who rose from humble beginnings, interwoven with six principles for career success.

...

Gurley cites Angela Duckworth's research on grit, which found that passion, not perseverance, is the harder element of sustained success. He offers practical tools including the Myers-Briggs personality test, scenario-planning frameworks from _Designing Your Life_ by Bill Burnett and Dave Evans, and immersive reading, and stresses it

...

The sixth principle, "Always Give Back," argues that generosity and mentorship should be practiced throughout one's career. Gurley frames careers as infinite games where many can succeed simultaneously and proposes measuring success by the number of other careers one has helped build.

Author Kris May

Bill Gurley, General Partner at Benchmark and one of the most influential venture capitalists of the last three decades has written a book and, in some ways, his recent visit to Questrom was… a book talk.
Runnin’ Down a Dream: How to Thrive in a Career You Actually Love tells the stories of those who have made it in their fields and outlines six principles to guide those who are in the process of choosing their own career path – one that you won’t end up regretting. Gurley talked about some of these principles with students.
Chase your curiosity . Gurley acknowledged that not everyone can achieve this, but ideally you want to find a job where continuous learning feels free. He said his book is full of obsessive learners and recommends finding your fascination and being a continuous learner. One final tip? It’s important to have both passion and perseverance because without passion, perseverance is simply suffering.
For those struggling to find their passion, Gurley recommends asking adults what they do for a living and then ask them to tell you three things they love about their job – and three things they hate about their job.
Gurley also talked about adopting an artisan approach. People with this approach exist in every field.
